done.what: (a) _partition: both sorted() calls (simple-graph and multigraph branches) now take iter(G.edges(data=True)), so sorted() no longer calls EdgeDataView.__len__ on the subgraph view, which walked the whole filtered adjacency. (b) cohesion_score: for a plain undirected nx.Graph (type(G) is nx.Graph and type(G._adj) is dict), the intra-community edge count is read from the adjacency dicts by the new _member_edge_counts/_intra_pair_edges instead of subgraph.number_of_edges() - number_of_selfloops(subgraph). DiGraph, multigraph, views and subclasses still take the original code. (c) The same count replaces subgraph.number_of_edges()==0 in _split_community (cluster.py:344-345, cited by the item), only for a plain Graph with a list argument. Each change is marked 'Local change (Verinoda)' and listed in the docs/UPSTREAM.md Modified table.
done.why_identical: (a) iter() drops only the length hint. The generator yields the same rows in the same order, because the view's __len__ changes nothing, and sorted() is stable. So edge_rows, the 'stable' graph and Leiden's input are the same. (b) The member set is set(G.nbunch_iter(nodes)), which is exactly what G.subgraph builds, with the same errors for an unhashable member and the same single-node handling. The sum over members of |N(u)&S| counts each non-loop edge twice and each self-loop once. The view's number_of_edges is (sum+loops)//2 because its degree counts a loop twice, and its self-loop count is loops. So the old value, number_of_edges minus self-loops, equals (sum-loops)//2: the same integer, hence the same float and the same <0.05 split decision. (c) The value is (sum+loops)//2, which is number_of_edges exactly. Proof on real graphs: a driver ran cluster, remap_communities_to_previous (twice, chained) and score_all on Graph, DiGraph and MultiGraph input, repr of the floats included, with baseline cc71f33 and with the new code under PYTHONHASHSEED 1 and 2. On the repo's graph.json (30,971 nodes, 73,325 edges, 2 self-loops, 1,036 communities), on a second real 30,971-node graph (scratchpad/stall/self, 1,081 communities) and on the orders example graph, all four outputs per graph are byte-identical (sha256 equal). Tests compare against the original code kept verbatim: random subsets with duplicates, absent nodes, tuple nodes and self-loops; cluster() end to end with the original counts forced by monkeypatching _plain_graph, including exclude_hubs; the stable graph handed to Leiden (node order, edge order, adjacency order); and a generated graph that reaches both the split and the cohesion paths.

done.what: remap_communities_to_previous: the O(old x new) set-intersection loop is replaced by _overlaps_by_count. It maps each node to its new community, walks previous_node_community once counting (old, new) pairs, and emits them old cid by old cid in first-appearance order, and within each old cid in communities order. The original loop is kept verbatim as _overlaps_by_intersection and is used as a fallback when a node appears in two new communities. The sort and the greedy matching are unchanged. Marked 'Local change (Verinoda)' and listed in the docs/UPSTREAM.md Modified table.
done.why_identical: |old_set & new_set| is the number of previous-map entries with that old cid whose node lies in that new community. This holds because the previous-map keys are distinct and each node is in at most one new community; duplicates across communities fall back to the original loop, and duplicates inside one community still count once. The overlaps list is built with the same tuples in the same order as the original loop, not just the same set, so even the sort's comparison sequence is unchanged. Tests: 400 randomized partitions and previous maps (absent nodes, non-contiguous cids, old cids with no overlap) assert the list from _overlaps_by_count == _overlaps_by_intersection and remap == the original function; plus the duplicate-node fallback, and remaps between clusterings of real-shaped graphs and their mutated copies. The real-graph driver (both hash seeds, base vs new) gives identical remapped output.

done.what: In-memory store of restored AST entries for long-lived processes. It is active only inside build_memo, and only in a process that has already finished a build (MCP index_update, watch), so a one-shot CLI update pays no pickling cost. The value is pickle.dumps of the entry after the source_file and id re-anchoring. The key is (entry path, id_restore, path_restore), checked against the entry's (st_size, st_mtime_ns, st_ino). A hit returns pickle.loads, a fresh object every time. An entry younger than the mtime granularity is not stored. At the end of each build only entries used in that build are kept. A pid guard stops a forked pool worker from storing. index.build enters the scope through index._cache_build_memo.
done.why_identical: The restored entry is a pure function of the entry bytes and the two restore anchors, and all three are in the key. The stat signature, including the inode (os.replace creates a new file), catches rewrites and deletions. The racy guard excludes same-tick rewrites. pickle round-trips JSON types, float bits, key order and surrogates exactly. Tests: three builds in one process across 4104 lookups each with results mutated between builds (scratch eq.py plus a unit test), 0 diffs against the upstream reference; rewritten and deleted entries are not served; young entries are not stored. defects: Verdict: not trustworthy. Inside .verinoda the comparison is tight: none of the clock, id, stamp, graph-mtime or date masks let a real difference through in my review, and a clean baseline-vs-baseline rerun exits 0. But all 9 new mutants changed something update writes and still exited 0. On top of that, a correct candidate that only changes extractor code fails through C0. Every mutant below was checked by hand to make sure its write really happens. Note that the harness deletes the work folder of an equal run, so the n3 leftover and n2 flag were lost along with it.

n1 (index/cache not compared, and the repository never moves), tools/update_equality.py:194 and 50-53 (one fixed folder). Mutant: project_index/cache.py no longer calls _relativize_ids_in, so AST cache entries keep absolute ids. Result: exit 0 on 21 orders steps. Real harm, shown outside the harness: after `scan` in folder firstplace/o, moving the repository and running `update` gives a graph.json with ids like firstplace_o_orders_api_get_repo. The baseline's graph has none. Fix: add a step that moves the store to a second fixed folder (for example <case>/r2/<corpus>) before an update. Also compare index/cache/ in warm mode, or at least compare the AST entries B and C write for the same file.

n2 (.git/index excluded), :946 GIT_UNCOMPARED_FILES. Mutant: after each update, `git update-index --skip-worktree -- tests/test_pricing.py`. Result: exit 0. git status stays clean, so from then on the user's edits to that file are hidden from git. Fix: add `git ls-files -v -s` (flags, mode, object id) and `git ls-files --debug`-free flags to git_state in corpus_items (:1805-1816).

n3 (writes outside the monitored folders), Env.run_env :1530-1545 and sweep_outside :1914. Mutant: update writes <repo>/../../eq_shared_cache.json (which is <case>/, not <case>/r/) and verinoda/_eq_memo.json inside the candidate checkout. Result: exit 0. USERPROFILE, HOME, APPDATA and LOCALAPPDATA are not redirected either. Fix: take a listing of the whole <case> tree except s/, t/ and the known folders before and after each run. Hash the candidate and baseline trees at start and end (excluding __pycache__). Point USERPROFILE, HOME, APPDATA and LOCALAPPDATA into the side's user folder.

n4 (build.lock excluded by name), :197. Mutant: update leaves its pid in .verinoda/build.lock, which the baseline leaves empty. Result: exit 0. Fix: exclude only the lock files' mtime, not their content. Compare size and bytes, since the baseline's build.lock is always empty.

n5 (SQLite compared by content only), sqlite_dump :826-879 (a documented limit). Mutant: a scratch table in atlas.db is created, filled with 200 KB and dropped. That leaves freelist 49 and a new schema_version. Result: exit 0. Fix: also compare PRAGMA page_count, freelist_count and schema_version. Or compare the raw bytes after a checkpoint on the copy, and keep the content diff only for the report.

n6 (NTFS alternate data streams), tree_state :919-937 (size, mtime and main-stream sha only). Mutant: snapshot.py writes the digest into '<file>:verinoda.sha256' of every freshly hashed source file and puts the mtime back. Result: exit 0; confirmed that the streams exist after a scan. Fix: on Windows, list each file's streams (FindFirstStreamW through ctypes) in the corpus and .verinoda listings, and compare them.

n7 (empty folders are invisible), tree_state :926-936 and tree_paths :1786-1792 list files only. Mutant: update leaves an empty .verinoda_tmp/ in the repository root and an empty .verinoda/index/staging/. Result: exit 0. Fix: add folders to both listings, as listing() at :955 already does.

n8 (file mode and attributes not compared), tree_state :935-936. Mutant: update makes tests/test_service.py read-only. Result: exit 0, and the user can no longer save that file. Fix: add st_mode and st_file_attributes to tree_state rows for the corpus.

n9 (only one update per process is ever run), step() :2121-2127 (CLI subprocess per update). Mutant: a process-wide memo on cache.file_hash keyed by path. It is exactly the kind of change rank 17/18 invite. Result: exit 0. Real harm, shown outside the harness: two updates in one process, the way the MCP index_update runs them. After the second edit the mutant's graph still has 42 nodes and lacks eq_second(); the baseline's has 43. Fix: add a side, or a step group, that runs consecutive updates inside one long-lived process (a driver calling workflow.update repeatedly, like mcp/server.py:1629), compared with B.

False positive (C0 cannot accept an extraction upgrade), make_c0 :2094-2105 and step :2139. Mutant fp: one comment line added to project_index/extractors/base.py, with no change in behaviour. Result: exit 1 at step noop, C0 only: `update_result $.untracked_citations`, `build_stats.json $.at <CLOCK run scan> != <CLOCK run noop>`, `atlas.db snapshots length 1 != 2`. Fix: when the probes' extraction stamps differ, build C0's reference from a copy of B whose build_stats extraction stamp is replaced, so the baseline also rebuilds.
